name: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
authors: Mirac Suzgun, Mert Yuksekgonul, Federico Bianchi, Dan Jurafsky, James Zou (Stanford University)
venue: EACL 2026 (Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics); arXiv preprint posted April 2025
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (the same black-box LM acts as a 'curator' that judges the usefulness/correctness of its own generated solutions and distills/prunes them into memory, prompted via task-agnostic instructions; no external verifier or learned critic). For code-heavy tasks the model can also self-validate via a Python interpreter, but the core curation signal is self-generated.
feedback_source: self-generated (the curator assesses correctness and generalizability of its own outputs without ground-truth labels or human feedback). Optionally augmented by an external Python interpreter for code-based tasks (Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer), but no ground-truth oracle is used.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine across a sequence of test queries (online-learning style): for each new query the generator answers conditioned on current memory, then the curator updates memory; this repeats query-by-query (inter-task accumulation rather than within-query retry). DC-RS additionally retrieves before answering.
reflection_object: reusable skill/workflow plus prompt/context: DC reflects on and curates a compact external text memory ('cheatsheet') of transferable strategies, problem-solving insights, heuristics, and reusable code snippets (e.g., a Python brute-force solver). It modifies the in-context memory artifact, not the model's reasoning chain in-place and not the model weights.
requires_training: none (no gradient updates; works on black-box LLM APIs such as GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet without modifying parameters)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (the same LM, prompted as a curator, decides what to store/refine/prune; no trained reward model, no verifiable reward, no ground-truth labels). For code tasks an interpreter can provide an execution-based check.
distillation_target: reusable-skill/workflow (and prompt): reflection is distilled into a self-curated, evolving cheatsheet of concise strategies, insights, and code snippets that persists in context and is reused across queries; explicitly NOT model-weights and NOT raw episodic transcripts.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the reflective/curation behavior is induced by task-agnostic prompts that define the Gen (generator) and Cur (curator) roles plus a retrieval mechanism; it is an external scaffold, not an RL-emergent capability. The behavior depends on the base model already having strong generative competence.
memory_type: playbook/cheatsheet (a self-curated, evolving external text memory of strategies, insights, and reusable code snippets); DC-RS additionally maintains a retrievable store of past input-output pairs
memory_persistence: cross-task (persists and accumulates across a sequence of distinct test queries within a benchmark / test-time stream). It is a test-time, online-learning memory rather than a productionized cross-session store, though it is designed to bridge isolated inference events.
memory_curation_mechanism: self-summarized/curated with overwrite/evolution: the LM curator (Cur) selectively (i) distills useful/generalizable solutions into compact entries, (ii) refines or removes incorrect/superseded entries, and (iii) consolidates for clarity and compactness to avoid context ballooning. DC-RS adds a retrieval-gated step (top-k=3 cosine-similarity retrieval over past input-output pairs via text-embedding-3-small) feeding the curator before generation.
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level (the curator judges whole candidate solutions as useful/correct or flawed and decides whether to store, refine, or prune the corresponding memory entry; errors are addressed at the level of strategies/solutions, not at step or token granularity).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: DC transfers distilled experience (strategies, code snippets, heuristics) across different test queries/problems; it does not iteratively refine a single answer within one query the way Self-Refine does.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only: corrections influence future queries (the curator prunes/refines faulty heuristics so later problems benefit); DC does not perform mid-trajectory in-flight recovery of the current answer, and there is no episodic retry-with-reset of the same query.
task_domains: math/competition reasoning, QA/reasoning (knowledge-intensive multiple-choice), heuristic-search arithmetic puzzles, tool-use (Python code generation/execution)
benchmarks: AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AIME 2020-2024, GPQA-Diamond, Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer, MMLU-Pro (Engineering and Physics)
headline_result: GPT-4o's Game of 24 accuracy jumped from 10% (baseline) to 99% under DC-RS after discovering and reusing a Python brute-force solver; Claude 3.5 Sonnet's AIME 2024 accuracy more than doubled from 23.3% to 50.0% (DC-Cu), with +30% on AIME 2025 (6.7% to 36.7%), all at inference time without weight updates or labels.
baselines: Baseline prompting (BL, vanilla minimal-instruction one-off inference); DC-empty (DC-no-memory, structured problem-solving + tool-use instructions but no retained memory, a strong baseline); Full-History appending (FH, raw uncurated transcript); Dynamic Retrieval (DR, retrieval of verbatim past pairs without curation); and Majority Voting (MV) over 3 samples.
gains_vs_baseline: vs strongest comparable baseline (DC-empty / DR, isolating the memory-curation effect): Game of 24 GPT-4o DC-RS 99% vs DC-empty 19% (+80); Claude Sonnet AIME 2024 DC-Cu 50.0% vs DC-empty 36.7% (+13.3, and +26.7 vs BL 23.3%); AIME 2025 Sonnet 36.7% (DC-Cu) vs 23.3% (DC-empty); GPQA-Diamond Sonnet 68.7% (DC-RS) vs 63.6% (DR) and 60.1% (DC-empty), +9.1 over BL; MMLU-Pro Physics Sonnet 82.0% vs 74.0% BL (+8); Math Equation Balancer Sonnet 44.8% BL to 98-100%. DC also beats FH (Sonnet AIME 2024: 50.0% DC vs 26.7% FH; GPT-4o FH degraded to 13.3% vs 40.0% DC-RS) and beats majority voting (MV gave no gain over BL on AIME).
compute_cost_profile: No gradient/training cost (black-box, no weight updates). Inference adds a curator call (and a retrieval step in DC-RS) after each query, so it is sequential and not trivially batchable. Output-token overhead grows but stays modest due to curation: on AIME 2024, Claude Sonnet averaged ~370 tokens (BL), 494 (DC-empty), 1035 (DC-RS), 1831 (DC-Cu) per query; over time it reduces redundant re-derivation (e.g., reusing a stored Python snippet), so curation becomes a net efficiency gain versus uncurated FH which blows up context length and cost.
known_limitations: Not a panacea: DC amplifies strong models but cannot fix foundational reasoning gaps. Smaller/weaker models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Haiku) gain little or even degrade because they produce too few correct solutions to seed memory and struggle to retrieve/refine entries (generative-competence and long-context-generation limits). Reasoning/'R1' models (DeepSeek R1, o1) showed minimal/inconsistent gains (outputs too verbose to curate). Faulty heuristics can be amplified if they enter memory; retrieval can introduce noise/confusion (GPT-4o dipped on GPQA-Diamond with bad retrieval); models sometimes abbreviate memory ('Previous content [...] preserved') degrading stored heuristics; sequential structure hampers large-scale parallel/batch inference; benefits are larger when test queries are structurally similar (curriculum/ordering matters).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only / self-verify: the curator has NO access to ground-truth labels or human feedback and must assess correctness/usefulness by itself. For code-amenable tasks (Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer) an external Python interpreter can verify execution, providing a quasi-verifiable signal, but DC's headline claim is that it works without ground-truth oracle labels.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent (and capacity-dependent): strongly net-positive for capable base models on tasks with structural regularity and code-amenable solutions (Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer, AIME, GPQA-Diamond for Claude), but net-neutral or slightly net-negative for GPT-4o on MMLU-Pro and GPQA-Diamond and for smaller/reasoning models, where curated memory can be noisy or misapplied. Improves without explicit label leakage.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report calibration/confidence metrics; it reports task accuracy. It does note risk of amplifying faulty heuristics and of overconfident-looking abbreviated memory updates, but no calibration analysis is given).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (Dynamic Cheatsheet is a memory/test-time-learning method, not a failure-attribution or failure-mode-classification method; it does not produce a failure taxonomy or attribute responsible steps/agents).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets repetitive re-derivation and re-committing of the same mistakes (e.g., recurring arithmetic errors) by reusing validated strategies/code; mitigates context ballooning from uncurated history. Self-acknowledged failure modes it can suffer: amplification of faulty heuristics (error propagation/loops), superficial/abbreviated self-reflection during curation, and retrieval noise; loosely maps to MAST-style issues such as error propagation and ineffective self-reflection, though the paper does not use MAST terminology.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark released, but the authors release all original input-output pairs and curated-memory artifacts in their codebase (github.com/suzgunmirac/dynamic-cheatsheet) for the evaluated tasks (AIME subsets, Game of 24 100-example set, Math Equation Balancer 250 expressions, GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro samples).
builds_on: Retrieval-augmented generation (Guu et al. REALM; Borgeaud et al. RETRO); in-context / online learning and test-time adaptation; self-reflection and self-refinement scaffolds (Reflexion, Self-Refine, Self-RAG); Tree/Graph-of-Thoughts style search (Yao et al. Game of 24, Besta et al.); STaR/self-taught reasoning and curriculum learning; Suzgun & Kalai (meta-prompting / 2024) for the Game of 24 setup.
extended_by_or_inspired: Agentic Context Engineering (ACE, Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models, Stanford/SambaNova 2025, OpenReview eC4ygDs02R) explicitly builds on Dynamic Cheatsheet's adaptive memory; Evo-Memory / ReMem (arXiv 2511.20857, benchmarking LLM-agent test-time learning with self-evolving memory) directly extends and benchmarks DC alongside Agent Workflow Memory; surveys on LLM agent memory (e.g., 'From Storage to Experience') and curated lists (Awesome-AI-Memory) cite it as a key memory-modules / experience-distillation method.
reasoning_model_native: No / negative result: DC is designed for black-box non-reasoning LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet). The authors explicitly tested reasoning/'R1' models (DeepSeek R1, o1) and found minimal or inconsistent gains because their outputs were too verbose to curate effectively, so DC does not hold well for o1/R1-style models with built-in reflection.
on_policy_distillation_link: Conceptually related to on-policy skill distillation but label-free: DC distills the model's own (on-policy) successful solutions/strategies into a reusable in-context skill library (cheatsheet) that conditions future generations, analogous to self-improvement via self-generated experience, but with NO gradient/weight distillation and NO ground-truth reward; it is verbal/in-context self-distillation into prompt-space rather than into model weights.
sample_efficiency: Online, no separate training phase: improvement accrues query-by-query over a single pass through the test stream (e.g., 30-250 examples per benchmark). Game of 24 shows a sharp jump early once the Python solver snippet is discovered and stored (then reused for the remaining ~100 examples); GPQA-Diamond improves gradually as snippets accumulate. No multi-trial retry per query is required.
